home.title: Vime: an offline multilingual keyboard
home.description: Vime is a fully offline multilingual keyboard for iOS that types Japanese, Chinese and English. Conversion, correction, learning and suggestions all run on your device.
home.tagline: A fully offline multilingual keyboard for iOS
home.intro: Japanese, Chinese and English in one keyboard. On-device models rank candidates, fix typos and suggest the next word, so what you type never leaves your phone.

points.title: Nothing leaves your device
points.text: Conversion, correction, learning and suggestions run on your phone. Vime contains no networking code.

points.title: Japanese, Chinese, English
points.text: Type Japanese in romaji or on the kana pad and Chinese in pinyin, Simplified or Traditional. Swipe up on the language key to switch.

points.title: On-device language models
points.text: Japanese and Chinese each have a small model that ranks candidates by what you wrote before.

points.title: Open source
points.text: Released under GPL-3.0-or-later; the code and the models are on GitHub.

sections.title: Whole sentences, adjustable segments
sections.text: A romaji QWERTY layout or the 12-key kana pad. Kana appear as you type while conversion updates in the background, never holding you up.
items: Sentence and segment conversion; − / + resize the first segment
Live conversion (ライブ変換) shows the converted text as you type
Undo a conversion: tap ↩ to go back to the reading
Correction candidates for neighbouring-key slips and similar sounds
Find Japanese kanji words by Chinese pinyin, such as jiancha → 検察

sections.title: Pinyin that reads the context
sections.text: Full pinyin built on librime, with an on-device Chinese model that picks the most natural of several sentences.
items: Whole sentences, initials-only abbreviations and unfinished syllables
Typo correction for neighbouring keys, swapped letters, and a missing or extra letter
After a short pause, checks the whole sentence for mistyped pinyin
Fuzzy pinyin, next-word suggestions, Simplified or Traditional
English words starting with a capital stay as typed in the sentence

sections.title: Everything close at hand
sections.text: Symbols, emoji and kaomoji in pages, with a bottom bar to switch and search. The first page shows Chinese or Japanese punctuation to match the input language.
items: A calculator on the number page: 1+1 → 2, 1+1=2
Auto-paired brackets with the cursor in between
Clipboard suggestions and a 24-hour history (off by default, on device only)
Swipe up on letter keys for symbols; slide across the keys to move the cursor

sections.title: Make it yours
sections.text: Built-in looks, or skins of your own with your images and colors, shared as .vimeskin files.
items: Drag to adjust the keyboard height
Key sounds and continuously adjustable haptics
One-handed mode in portrait, left or right
VoiceOver, larger text, bold text and increased contrast

sections.title: Clear settings, learning you control
sections.text: Setup takes three steps, and the typing page offers Japanese or Chinese practice to match the input language.
items: Choose Japanese romaji, the kana pad and Simplified Chinese on the Input Methods page
Separate Japanese and Chinese user dictionaries, with import and export
Review and delete words learned from pinyin, or clear all learning at once
Interface in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, English and Korean

status.title: Version status
status.next_note: Next version on the dev branch
rhythm: Changes are merged into the development branch at any time.
**Tuesday to Thursday 19:00 UTC** (Wednesday to Friday 03:00 in Beijing): when the development branch has new changes, a beta is built and uploaded to TestFlight, once a day.
The latest TestFlight build is checked and the release notes are written.

Once the build is checked and the screenshots are ready, it is submitted for App Store review by hand and released automatically once approved. While features change often, there is no fixed submission day.
